tasks.title: CLP/JPY/KWD amounts rendered with the wrong number of decimals
tasks.summary: Fixed Amount.Decimal() in money/amount.go. It hardcoded 2 decimals (/100, %02d), so CLP/JPY showed 15000 as "150.00" and KWD showed 1.234 as "12.34". It now uses the currency's Exponent: 0 decimals for CLP/JPY, 3 for KWD, 2 for USD/EUR/etc. Negative amounts keep the minus sign, and the negation uses uint64 so MinInt64 doesn't overflow. The API responses (payment, refund, list) and the webhook payloads all render amounts through Decimal(), so they pick up the fix. Money.Fee works in minor units and needed no change. I added money/decimal_test.go covering CLP/JPY/KWD/USD/EUR, negatives, and a Parse round trip. All tests pass with -race, and gofmt reports nothing.

tasks.title: Multiple partial refunds can exceed the captured amount
tasks.summary: Fixed the over-refund bug in payment/service.go. Refund compared the requested amount to the full payment amount, so it ignored earlier refunds. It now compares against the remaining amount (Amount − Refunded). A refund larger than what's left returns ErrRefundExceedsRemaining, which the API maps to 422 refund_exceeds_remaining, and the payment is left unchanged. Refunding exactly the remaining amount still moves the payment to REFUNDED. The existing test suite and go vet pass with -race. I didn't add a regression test for the 600 + 600 on 1000.00 case. For concurrent refunds on the same payment, optimistic locking already rejects a stale write with 409 conflict, so the total can't exceed the payment amount that way either.

tasks.title: Cursor pagination silently drops one payment per page
tasks.summary: Fixed an off-by-one in store/memory.go ListByMerchant. The cursor already encodes the next offset (`end`), but the decoder added 1 more, so one payment was skipped at every page boundary. That gave 981 of 1000 payments at limit=50 and about half at limit=1. I removed the extra `offset++`. The last page still returns an empty next_cursor, including when the total is an exact multiple of the limit. I added store/paging_test.go, a regression test that walks every page and checks each payment appears once, in creation order. It covers 1000 payments at limit 50, limit 1, an exact multiple, and an empty merchant. The existing suite, `go vet` and `go test -race` all pass; I didn't run `gofmt -l .`.

tasks.title: Webhook dispatcher retries permanent 4xx failures and gives up on 5xx
tasks.summary:
Fixed `retryable` in webhook/dispatcher.go so it matches the README policy. Transport errors, 408, 429 and 5xx are now retried. Every other non-2xx status, including 400/401/404/410, is permanent and goes straight to the dead-letter list. Previously 4xx was retried and 5xx was not, which is why m_77's endpoint kept getting POSTs and m_91's events were dead-lettered after one attempt.

I also made the dispatcher treat `MaxAttempts` below 1 as 1. Before, that case recorded a dead letter with an attempt count of 1 even though nothing had been sent. Dead letters already recorded `Attempts` and `LastStatus` correctly, so I left that code alone.

The existing webhook tests pass with `-race`, and `gofmt -l .` is clean. I didn't add new tests for the 410 and 503 cases. I didn't run `go vet` or the other packages' tests either.

tasks.title: Idempotency keys never expire after 24h
tasks.summary: Fixed idempotency/store.go. Begin now treats a record as expired when now >= ExpiresAt. It deletes the record and starts a new request whatever the fingerprint. The purge condition was wrong: it required now - ExpiresAt > ttl, so records lived about 2×TTL (~48h). It now evicts when !now.Before(ExpiresAt). Len also runs the purge, which is still throttled to once per minute. The existing tests, gofmt and the build pass. I didn't add new tests for the expiry cases.

tasks.title: Every client error is returned as 500 internal_error
tasks.summary:
The cause was in `api/errors.go`. `errorResponse` used `switch err { case payment.ErrNotFound: ... }`, which compares errors by identity. Since last week's release the service wraps every error with `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)`, so nothing matched and everything fell through to 500. I changed it to a tagless `switch` that uses `errors.Is` for every sentinel, and added the `errors` import. The sentinels are the payment errors plus the money errors. The statuses and codes are unchanged and match the README. Unrecognised errors still return 500 with the generic "internal error" message.

This one fix covers all four cases in the ticket (404, 409, 422 and 400). Malformed bodies are covered because `decodeJSON` wraps `ErrInvalidInput`. The idempotent create and refund paths go through the same function.

`go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt -l .` all pass. I didn't add a regression test for the wrapped-error cases.

`payment.ErrDuplicate` still has no mapping, so it returns 500. The README doesn't document a code for it, so I left it alone.

tasks.title: Late webhook retries fire with no delay
tasks.summary: Fixed Policy.Backoff in webhook/dispatcher.go. The old `BaseDelay << (n-1)` overflowed int64 for large attempt numbers (around attempt 30 or more with a 1s base), which made the delay zero or negative. The new version doubles step by step and returns MaxDelay as soon as the next doubling would pass it. The delay is therefore monotonic and capped at MaxDelay, and it can't overflow. It also treats n<1 as 1. The existing webhook tests pass. I didn't add a new test for the 48-attempt case.

tasks.title: Add payment cancellation (CANCELED status + endpoint + webhook)
tasks.summary:
Added payment.StatusCanceled ("CANCELED"). It is final and accepted by ParseStatus. Added Service.Cancel, allowed from CREATED and PENDING only. Any other state fails with ErrInvalidTransition, and an unknown id fails with ErrNotFound. A successful cancel emits "payment.canceled", which the existing dispatcher delivers as a webhook. Added POST /payments/{id}/cancel, which returns 200 with the payment body, 409 invalid_transition or 404 not_found. Authorize, Capture, Decline and Refund already reject any other status, so a canceled payment gets 409 from all of them. I also updated the lifecycle section of the README.

`go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are clean. I did not add tests for Cancel or the new endpoint, so the new code is covered only by the existing suite and whatever hidden acceptance tests you run.

`gofmt -l` flagged `payment/payment.go` after my edits, and I couldn't see why. I rewrote the file in full, with `Final()` on multiple lines, and it passes now.

tasks.title: Filter the merchant payment listing by status
tasks.summary:
Added an optional `status` filter to GET /merchants/{merchantID}/payments.
- `payment.Page` has a new `Status` field. An empty value means no filter.
- The handler parses `status` with `payment.ParseStatus`, so matching is case-insensitive. An unknown value returns 400 `invalid_request`.
- `store.Memory.ListByMerchant` now scans the merchant's payments in creation order and collects up to `limit` matches, so every page except the last is full.
- The cursor is a position in the unfiltered list. `next_cursor` is only set when a later match exists, so it is empty after the last match.
- Without `status` the results are the same as before.
- The existing suite passes with `-race`, and `gofmt` is clean.
- I added no tests for the new filter.
- `?status=` with an empty value is treated as no filter rather than a 400.

tasks.title: Replay a dead-lettered webhook event
tasks.summary:
Added `Dispatcher.Replay` and `webhook.ErrDeadLetterNotFound` in `webhook/dispatcher.go`. Added `POST /webhooks/dead-letters/{eventID}/replay`. `go vet`, `gofmt` and `go test -race ./...` pass. I didn't add tests for `Replay` or the new route.

- **How `Replay` works:** it removes the event from the dead-letter list and re-delivers it with the same event id and payload under the normal retry policy. The signature is recomputed on each send. I split the delivery loop into a helper that reports what happened, so `Flush` behaves as before.
- **Results:** on success it returns `(true, nil)`. If delivery fails again, it returns `(false, nil)` and the event is in the list once, with the new attempts and status. An unknown id returns an error wrapping `ErrDeadLetterNotFound`.
- **HTTP:** the route returns 200 `{"event_id", "delivered"}`. Unknown ids map to 404 `not_found`.
- **Cancelled context:** if the context is cancelled mid-delivery, the original dead letter goes back in its old position and the error is returned.
- **No endpoint configured:** if the merchant no longer has an endpoint, the original dead letter is also restored. In that case `Replay` returns `(false, nil)`, and the API reports `delivered: false`. The ticket didn't cover this case, so say if you want different behaviour.

tasks.title: Accept and return integer minor units, backward compatible
tasks.summary:
POST /payments and POST /payments/{id}/refunds now accept `amount_minor` (integer minor units) as well as the legacy `amount` string. This is done by a new `resolveAmount` helper in `api/handlers.go`. Payment responses gain `amount_minor`, `fee_minor`, `refunded_minor` and `remaining_minor`, and each refund gains `amount_minor`. The existing test suite, `go vet` and `gofmt` pass. I did not add tests for the new behaviour or run with `-race`.

- **Request rules:** If neither field is present, the API returns 400 `invalid_request`. If both are present and they disagree, it also returns 400 `invalid_request`. A null value counts as absent. A fractional `amount_minor` such as `10.5` fails JSON decoding and returns 400.
- **Idempotency:** The fingerprints were already built from minor units and currency, so a retry in the other format with the same amount is replayed. I didn't change them.
- **Responses:** The new fields come from the shared `toPaymentResponse`, so every endpoint that returns a payment, including list, has them. Existing fields are unchanged.
- **Unknown fields:** Still rejected, because `decodeJSON` is untouched.
- **Webhooks:** I didn't touch webhook payloads, since the ticket only covers the API.

I left `maxBodyBytes`, `decodeJSON` and the service layer alone. The changes are in `api/dto.go` and `api/handlers.go`.

tasks.title: Centralize the payment status machine in one transition table
tasks.summary: Added `payment.CanTransition(from, to Status) bool`, backed by a single transitions table in payment/payment.go. It allows CREATED→PENDING/DECLINED, PENDING→SUCCEEDED/DECLINED and SUCCEEDED→REFUNDED, and nothing else (no self transitions, unknown statuses return false). `Status.Final()` is now derived from the same table, so it no longer hardcodes statuses. Authorize, Capture, Decline and Refund in payment/service.go now validate through `CanTransition`, and every `switch p.Status` is gone. Refund gates on `CanTransition(status, REFUNDED)`, so a partial refund is allowed exactly when a full one would be. Error messages, events and the order of checks (status, then currency, then remaining amount) are unchanged. `go test ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are clean. I didn't run `go vet` or `go test -race`.

tasks.title: Idempotency store is not safe under concurrent retries
tasks.summary: Fixed idempotency.Memory concurrency. Begin now holds the mutex for the whole check-and-insert, so only one concurrent caller per key can start. Previously it unlocked between the lookup and the insert, which allowed duplicate refunds. Complete and Release now take the lock for their map access and record mutation, which removes the concurrent map read/write crash and the data race. `go test -race ./...` passes; I didn't add a new concurrent test.

tasks.title: In-memory repository shares mutable state with callers
tasks.summary: Root cause: store.Memory kept and returned payments by value, but Payment.Refunds is a slice, so the stored payment and the copies shared a backing array. Concurrent Refund calls appended into that shared array, which caused the data race and the phantom refund entries from calls that later lost with a version conflict. Fixes: Memory.Create, Get, Update and ListByMerchant now deep-copy with Payment.Clone, so nothing mutable is shared in or out. Optimistic-locking behaviour is unchanged. Payment.Clone preserves a nil Refunds slice. In the service, events now get a cloned Payment and a copied Refund, so publisher consumers don't share state with the value returned to the caller. `go test -race ./...` passes. I didn't add a new concurrent-refund test.

tasks.title: Idempotency Begin gets slower with every stored key
tasks.summary:
Fixed Memory.Begin in idempotency/store.go. It was copying and sorting every record on each call (O(n log n)), which is why latency grew with the number of stored keys. Eviction is now a single map scan that runs at most once per minute (`purgeInterval`, tracked by a new `lastPurge` field). Begin's lookup still checks `now.Before(ExpiresAt)`, so expired keys are never replayed between scans, and expired records are still evicted, so memory stays bounded. I removed the unused `sort` import. The existing tests, gofmt and `go test ./...` pass. I did not add a benchmark or a new test for the once-per-minute eviction, and I did not run `go vet`.

The one Begin call per minute that triggers the scan still costs O(n). That fits the ticket's "at most once per minute" allowance, but it means that call is slower than the rest.

tasks.title: Split payouts do not reconcile with the charged amount
tasks.summary:
I rewrote `money.Allocate` in `money/allocate.go` so the parts always add up to the charge. The existing tests, `go vet` and `gofmt` pass. I didn't add new tests, so your three examples (100.00 ÷ 3, 0.10 ÷ 7, 0.05 ÷ 2) haven't been run against the fix.

The old code rounded each share independently with floats, which is why splits came out short or over. The new version works in exact integer arithmetic:
- Each part gets the exact floor of its proportional share.
- The leftover cents go one each to the parts with the largest remainder, ties going to the lower index, as the doc comment promises.
- The multiplication uses `math/bits` 128-bit math, so large amounts can't overflow it.
- It returns an error if the ratios sum past `int64`.

By the contract, 100.00 ÷ 3 now gives 33.34, 33.33, 33.33.

tasks.title: Identical retries rejected as idempotency key reuse
tasks.summary:
The idempotency fingerprint now hashes the parsed request instead of the raw body, so a retry that re-serializes the same request replays the original response. Existing tests, `go vet` and gofmt pass. I didn't add a test for the retry case from the ticket.

The fingerprint was a hash of the raw JSON body, so key order, whitespace, `10.5` vs `10.50` and `usd` vs `USD` all counted as a different request. The new `semanticFingerprint` in `api/idempotency.go` replaces `bodyFingerprint` and hashes these fields:
- **Path:** the request path.
- **Amount:** the amount in minor units, which makes `10.5` and `10.50` equal.
- **Currency:** the upper-cased currency code, so `usd` and `USD` match.
- **Merchant:** `merchant_id`, for payment creation only.

In `api/handlers.go`, `createPayment` and `refundPayment` now compute the fingerprint after decoding and parsing the amount. For refunds, `{"amount":"5.00"}` and `{"amount":"5"}` now match.

A reused key with a genuinely different request (different merchant, amount or currency) still gets 422 `idempotency_key_reused`.

One behaviour change: a malformed body or an invalid amount is now rejected before any idempotency lookup. It was already rejected before the operation ran, so nothing that used to succeed is affected.

tasks.title: Processing fees overcharged by one cent
tasks.summary: Fixed money.Fee. It used float64 math.Ceil, which always rounded up and lost precision on large amounts. It now computes amount×bps exactly with a 128-bit product (math/bits Mul64/Div64) and rounds half-to-even, as the doc comment says. The 10.05 USD at 290 bps case now gives 0.29, and amounts up to MaxInt64 are handled without overflow. Existing tests, go vet and gofmt pass. I didn't add new tests.
